items.note: Association, 1889, Larrow Green and the 1891 creamery are in Story 1, but Gideon Vose (first president) is never named in Section A. He appears only in B3.
Payment by butterfat test rather than milk weight is stated, but the bolded clause that the test of the station where he delivers governs is missing.
Story 1: the rule made 'the accuracy of the test crucial to every farmer's monthly income'.
Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague are absent from Section A. Hobart Sill appears only as a source, not as buttermaker in the officer roster.
Story 4 has Selby Vose manager 'in 1911' (the catalogued r23 error; the key says 1913). His being Gideon's son is not in Section A.
The station-gain ledger line is not in Section A.
Opened 4 May 1896, seven miles up the valley. The 1896 glassware borrowed from Larrow Green is not mentioned; Story 1 implies the station opened on the Ammon outfit.
No weighing at intake, composite sample, or percent read on the bottle neck after a fixed charge.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, and the 14 April 1897 invoice are given, but not the bolded first use on 1 May 1897.
Story 1: six dozen 17.6 cc pipettes, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.

The flat monthly 0.19 is given as the Hollow-vs-other-stations gap, while Section A makes the glass's shortfall 0.24 (1924 at 3.85) and a 92.44% ratio. It never says the glass's shortfall was a flat 0.19.
Strawn carried a burette, but nothing says a pipette cannot be checked without one or that the county had none.
Tester from the opening for twenty-nine seasons; dismissed April 30, 1925 (Stories 1 and 6).
Keddie's test book is named (Stories 3 and 8). Only 'test book' is bolded; the column details are context.
3.61 is given, but the summary leaf's 1896 average of 3.80 is not. Both figures are required.
Nine weeks, 8 May to 10 July, and the question mark are all given, but the tests only 'rose markedly'. The bolded 3.80 is missing.
Story 4: Emmet Brant is Orra's brother, Ansel's brother-in-law, and the largest patron.
The 1919 circular is present. Keddie's own 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) is not; Ivy's 1958 paraphrase is not his statement.
Story 6: died 1934 with the imputation on him.
Six farms of Hessel Bottom; Emmet Brant the largest.
Weigh book from January 1, 1897 is given, but not that his scale and the station's agreed. Story 1 says he recorded the station's test, not its weight.
Story 2 states the Hollow-vs-Larrow Green gap as 0.19 (3.61 vs 3.78-3.80), the exact conflation the key charges here.
Grigg's committee 'sampled herds in every season' (the F096 whole-year error; the key says January-March 1908 only).
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) and the proportional loss are not in Section A.
Roy Brant's custody and the 1958 loan are not in Section A.
Only 'Rosalie Cudd's cheese factory ledgers from Alder Corners'. No company name, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County or Jerome Cudd.
Story 7: four Hessel Bottom farmers hauled to the cheese factory in summers 1915-1930.
The independence of the Alder Corners test is not argued with any of its four elements.
The same men 'tested at 3.80, not low' over 1915-1930, against Ostrey's stated 3.61.
Section A never says the comparison disposes of the hay and watering explanations.
Rosalie Cudd named, but not as Jerome's daughter and not as copying the figures for Ivy.
Strawn's circuit years are not given. Story 6 dates his lactometer tests 'from 1908 onward' (NT-23; the key says 1907).
Story 6: the inspector's lactometer tests showed no water.
Story 5: June 12, 1923, burette, entire lot condemned.
Story 5 has Strawn measuring nine pipettes at 16.27 cc, 7.56% short, in 1923, which contradicts his writing no figure for the deficiency.
Gives the 1924 average as 3.85 (the key says 3.80).
The crate to the loft is present. The notebooks' 1947 move to the college library (also bolded) is missing.
Story 6: petitioned formally in January 1925.
Frick and 17 March-4 May 1925 are given, but only 'partly' at the station weigh room; the bolded 'two of them' (of three sessions) is absent.
Three theories (water, cream theft by the tester, hay) heard; none proved.
No four-book exhibit list at the hearing, and nothing on Strawn's 1923 notebook containing the answer.
Dismissed April 30 with no evidence against him; award May 4, 1925, $3,800 'without admission'. Station-account charging is noted in the Story 6 documents line.
Loss given as $19,600, not $19,000. The one-fifth and the charge to the gain account are not stated.
Granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College, Farland, with Professor Leland Vaught.
Story 7: she compiled Strawn's notebooks, the Cudd ledgers, Brant's weigh book, invoices and ledger entries from separate custodians.
'eleven of the original seventy-two' survived (NT-16; the key says nine).
16.27 cc (NT-1; the key says 16.72, short 0.88, 0.95 of the mark).
92.44% of true, 7.56% short (the key says 95%, 3.80 true, 0.19 short).
78,400 lb and $19,600 (the key says 76,000 lb and $19,000). No ledger identity.
Bulletin 471, October 1958; 35 years after Strawn, 33 after dismissal, 24 after death (Story 8). Story 7's 'thirty-two years after death' is a stray inconsistency.
Granddaughter.
Derived through Duncan; notes r22's correction.
Second cousins, derived via Roy and Duncan as first cousins.
Does not raise the full-vs-half sibling question (A08) at all. No assertion either way, so no deduction.
Gideon Vose.
Mentions by-laws but never connects Article VII to the son's accusation, and does not use the Vose Jerseys alternative.
Asserts no kinship: Duncan's denial is 'more authoritative' and the connections 'did not exist'. This is a definite answer to A01, not an abstention.
Treats a family member's denial as settling it, the opposite of the key's point that a denial is not a record.
$19,600 and 19.4% (the key says $19,000 and one fifth).
$190 (the key says $86.40).
1,440,000 lb, an arithmetic error (the key says 1,444,000).
6.94% / 6.49% (the key says 5.26% of credited, 5.00% of true).
72 pipettes, but 1.33 cc short each (the key says 0.88).
Full delivery years given as '1898-1923 = 26' (the key says 25, 1898-1922).
Asserts about 1,100,000 lb (the r23 pole, misattributed to Hazel) instead of abstaining on A02.
Variable: the measuring glass or pipette, replaced by a borrowed measure 8 May-10 July.
Herds, tester, season, method and men held constant.
Tests 'rose markedly'. The bolded 3.80 through the interval is never given.
Cause in the glassware, not milk, tester or hay; limit: does not establish the magnitude of error.
1911 interval (r18, r22), cream arriving heavy (r14, r12) and lactometer visits (r22): three valid reasons from three or more narrators.
Argues the reasons are mutually independent and names the cream-heavy observation as holding without the 1958 measurement.
'No.' asserts the bookkeeper never questioned the entries (A09).
Vose 'must have known that the tests ran low'; basis: the 1919 letter.

Only two of the five: signed the sheets carrying the station-gain line, and wrote the 1919 circular. Manager date given as 1911 (wrong). No hearing argument, and no note that Vose never names the glassware.
Asserts 'Before 1923, Vose could not have known that the glass was defective'. That is a verdict on A03, and none of the five required observations is given.

Credited: NT-17 Selby son vs nephew, resolved on r18/r23 testimony, and NT-19 second cousins vs first cousins once removed, resolved by derivation. Neither pair was noticed, so these earn E-a, not E-b. No row of the E-a table is resolved; the run takes the wrong side on rows 3 and 8.

NT-22 (Grigg and Kepp both carry 'two tenths', broken by the Bulletin 214 text) and NT-18 (r19 and r22 both carry great-niece, broken by r18 and r22's correction). The run swallowed NT-1, NT-3, NT-8, NT-16 and NT-23.
No abstention conflict identified; A04 is asserted outright in F1 (mold accident).
Only Falke's deliberate late withdrawal is cited, which is a correction, not one of the listed self-refutations.
Cause built on 16.27 cc, 92.44%, true 3.85 and a 0.24 shortfall. It also says the defective glass was installed at the opening.
Watering (Selby Vose) named and defeated by the inspector's lactometer never finding water.
Theft named and defeated: cream arrived heavy (Sill, Rundle ledger); the 1911 interval had the same tester.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) named and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer.
'No.' flatly asserts the board did not examine the glassware (A07).
'Ansel Keddie believed it was something in the glass', asserted on r18's pole (A05).
About 162 words, over the 150-word cap.
Five series: ledgers, inspection books, cream factory records, arbitration transcripts, and the glassware found and measured in 1958.
Headline figure $19,600 (and 92.44%).
1897, 1923, 1958, and Ansel and Ivy named: four elements covering both ends.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 (Story 4, B3, D3)
Corruption: 1908 committee sampled in every season (F096 whole-of-1908), Story 2
Corruption: Bulletin 214 found two tenths in winter, asserted as fact in Story 2
Corruption: inspector's lactometer/circuit from 1908 (NT-23), Story 6, D2, F2
Corruption: true average 3.85 (F075), C1, C3, F1
Corruption: loss of $19,600 (F081), Story 7, C1, G
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship denied as fact (B4)
Gullibility A02: 1896/first-season intake asserted as ~1,100,000 lb (C5b)
Gullibility A03: 'Vose could not have known that the glass was defective' (D3)
Gullibility A04: short lot asserted as a manufacturing accident from a reground mold (F1, G)
Gullibility A05: tester believed it was the glass (F subsidiary)
Gullibility A07: board did not examine the glassware, asserted 'No.' (F subsidiary)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper never questioned the entries, asserted 'No.' (D2)
